To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a theoretical framework for base station (BS) energy saving, which encompasses dynamic BS operation (i.e., on/off switching) and user association together; 2) we propose optimal user association policies that minimize the total cost, which allows for a flexible energy-performance tradeoff; 3) for the BS operation problem, we develop simple greedy algorithms, and further propose other practical heuristics that do not require any additional signaling overhead.
we develop a framework for energy-efficient BS operation that encompasses dynamic BS switching and the related problem on optimal user association.
the proposed user and base station association mechanisms can achieve energy savings up to 30% and 60%, respectively, while maintaining the same performance level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the joint optimization of BS operation and user association for energy saving.
a novel and challenging problem of jointly optimizing BS operation and user association for energy saving in green cellular networks.
the fundamental tradeoffs between energy consumption and flow-level performance in cellular networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, by jointly optimizing the user association and BS switching on/off, the proposed schemes can reduce the energy consumption by up to 50% with only 5% degradation in flow-level performance.
the proposed user-association and BS-operation mechanisms provide significant energy savings while maintaining the flow-level performance.
the proposed algorithms can significantly reduce the total energy consumption in a green cellular network, while maintaining a reasonable flow-level performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a novel theoretical framework for BS operation and user association in cellular networks, which allows a flexible tradeoff of flow-level performance and network energy efficiency.
, by jointly considering BS operation and user association, we can achieve a better energy saving performance than those obtained by separately optimizing each of these two mechanisms.
we propose an optimal user association algorithm that minimizes energy consumption and provides a flexible tradeoff with the performance metric of interest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
energy-efficient BS operation and user association are highly complementary, and thus, should be jointly considered in future green cellular network designs.
energy-efficiency can be significantly improved by jointly optimizing user association and BS operations.
the energy consumption of cellular networks can be significantly reduced without sacrificing performance by carefully considering both the user association problem and the BS operation problem.
